subject: general
question: Generally, the value of MPC (Marginal Propensity to Consume) ________.

options.text: does not exceed 1 or fall below 0

solution:
The correct answer is __**does not exceed 1 or fall below 0**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In economics, the **marginal propensity to consume** (MPC) is defined as the proportion of an aggregate raise in pay that a consumer spends on the consumption of goods and services, as opposed to saving it.
 
• Marginal propensity to consume is a component of **Keynesian macroeconomic theory** and is calculated as the change in consumption divided by the change in income.
 
• Marginal Propensity to Consume is the proportion of an increase in income that gets **spent on consumption**.
 
• MPC is the key determinant of the Keynesian multiplier, which describes the effect of increased investment or government spending as an **economic stimulus**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **In Keynesian macroeconomic theory,** the marginal propensity to consume is a key variable in showing the multiplier effect of economic stimulus spending.
 
• To calculate the marginal propensity to consume, the change in consumption is divided by the **change in income**.
 
• The marginal propensity to consume measures the degree to which a consumer will spend or **save in relation to an aggregate raise in pay**.
 
• According to Keynesian theory, an increase in investment or government spending increases consumers’ income, and they will then spend more.
